thread:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — console showed another workspace's quota graph for ~2s when I rapidly switched workspaces just now. Repro steps below, can reproduce on prod.
Maria Gomez: I saw that too a minute ago. Happened after the edge proxy roll yesterday? :thinking_face:
Tony Li: probably an edge prefetch / cache key mismatch. Can you dump the request/response headers when it happens?
Alex Chen: capture attached:
```http
GET /api/console/quota?range=30d HTTP/1.1
Host: console.redwood.internal
X-Workspace-ID: workspace-b
X-Request-ID: req-79a2
Edge-Cache-Key: pref:worksp:workspace-a:metrics:30d
X-Internal-Route: /internal/metrics?org=workspace-a
Cache-Control: max-age=60
```
Maria Gomez: interesting — `Edge-Cache-Key` is built with `workspace-a` even though `X-Workspace-ID` is `workspace-b`.
Elaine Park: that suggests the prefetch that populated the edge cache used a different internal call to render the gauge and the proxy used values from that call to compute the cache key. Race on rapid switch.
Sam Riley: telemetry spike aligns: see increased cache hits with mismatched `X-Workspace-ID` 2026-03-15T04:12Z — pulling query now.
Tony Li: short-term mitigation options:
- scrub internal headers like `X-Internal-Route` and `X-Org` at the edge before generating cache keys
- or include `X-Workspace-ID` explicitly in the cache key
I lean towards scrubbing to avoid leaking internal route hints into cache keys.
Maria Gomez: we should also audit exposure window (how many workspaces were shown wrong). It's quota numbers (not PII) but it's tenant leakage — need SOC aware.
Alex Chen: agreed. Hotfix proposal: disable caching for `/api/console/quota` at edge for 24h and deploy header-scrub rule. Then push proper fix in proxy code.
Tony Li: will open PR for header scrub + unit tests. Hotfix ETA: 4h to push staging change, 8h for prod if no issues. Full code fix ETA: 24-48h.
Elaine Park: also adding a regression in the canary harness: a script that does 100 rapid workspace toggles and asserts visible metrics correspond to the selected workspace.
telemetry-bot: query results: 312 anomalous cache hits with mismatched workspace IDs in the last 6h (peak at 04:12UTC).
deploy-bot: Edge proxy rollout 0.4.13 started at 2026-03-15T04:10:22Z; Canary at 10%.
Sam Riley: timeline lines up with canary ramp. Likely a change in how the proxy calculated prefetched cache keys for affinity-prefetch.
Alex Chen: action items / owners:
- Tony Li: edge header-scrub hotfix + PR (owner). Add revert plan. (Tony please comment with PR link)
- Maria Gomez: audit exposure & notify SOC, create ticket INC-1234 (owner)
- Elaine Park: add canary regression test (owner)
- Sam Riley: telemetry query + dashboard to monitor recurrence (owner)
Tony Li: revert plan = immediate rollback of proxy config + disable prefetch rule; I'll include an automated rollback step in the hotfix playbook.
Maria Gomez: I've created INC-1234 and pinged security on Slack. Added brief note: "quota telemetry leakage window".
Tony Li: pushed hotfix to staging, running smoke tests now. I'll tag the PR here when ready.
Elaine Park: creating test ticket CASE-998 with steps + expected asserts.
Alex Chen: thanks everyone. Once hotfix is live let's run long-run canary toggles and then re-enable caching gradually. :thumbsup:
Maria Gomez: FYI — if anyone finds similar for other console endpoints (insights/panels) please post.
Tony Li: PR: https://git.redwood/edge/proxy/pulls/456 (WIP) — will update status.
telemetry-bot: note: included metric `edge.cache.mismatch.workspace` added to the dashboard under "console -> cache anomalies".
Sam Riley: monitoring set. I'll keep an eye and escalate if counts don't drop after hotfix.
Alex Chen: cool. tagging this thread for postmortem notes later.
